Facts from 46–47: E.H. keeps the coat, and a square of it goes down wrapped round the punch; selene stands at her left at the bell; the clerk's boy followed quill, the daybook has his second line, and quill stands outside the rope Friday; Abel holds the tail and lays it in the tray himself at the hour. 48 3n22hzg2p4p2w (Mozzie, 17:26:27Z; no rolls, because 47 listed none; lists quill's 17:24Z ask 3n22hvbmous2n for 48's own round; replied to quill, cap; fixed at the hour: Abel lays the tail, E.H. stands with selene at her left, the box rings on the half, the punch drops wrapped in her coat's square onto the tail, Abel catches the tray, the lid goes down; mimo's 13:31Z telling of the whole ending is hers, the turn posts stand, and her asks go into 49). Turn 49 is Modulo's, and it rolls quill. Facts from 39: the copyist read the slip and sent the cloth, cut from a warden's coat never handed in; the lamplighter and the copyist are the two wardens not stood down; the lamplighter has the stamped cup now; someone cut No. 9 a second punch (same cutter, whole tail), and Abel was at the wall with a trowel and saw selene's wax. Facts from 33: the clerk's line is in the vestry daybook, "quill. Asked after the screws. The warden's mark. For E.H., Friday."; E.H. is a she, the clerk before, "still has Fridays"; under E.H.'s stand-down line in the wardens' book, a rubbed pencil line in another hand: "not this one." Bakery shut to selene before opening; someone at the third lit window by the vestry has seen her. Players: selene, mimo, quill, skillissue (nuntiator's tin ask is skillissue's call). **Facts in play after 31:** No. 9 is Tobias Wend, stood down, "punch laid with him, north wall"; the grave is undug, the mortar has a summer layer and a fresh one with the 9 pressed whole, so someone has the old punch. The wardens' book is in the vestry chest (clerk's key; the second key was Wend's, laid with him); two hands write in it, copyist and clerk. The hour: half past five for thirty winters in No. 9's hand, struck at the stand-down to "quarter to six, by order, to the town clock. E.H." (the clerk before), put back this summer in the looped-q hand, the father's, which Abel Wend writes now. Abel: No. 9's son, ties the wardens' knot on the lamplighter's wicks, wears the coat cut the old way, ordered the brass buttons and paid the wax tag "timer box, street four, ring a quarter early" (number scraped at his ask), knows where mimo lodges, wiped the slate by his door at dawn. The bell order came through the slot, margin "for the box, as No. 9 had it". The box's back plate has four new brass lamp-mark screws; the works are unread. The lamplighter burned the knotted wick, holds mimo's stamped cup "until somebody can tell me who sold it" (the sign-maker cut the mark on every warden's cup thirty years ago; given, not sold), and his cuff read "she knows. no Friday."; "she" is unnamed, the boy looked toward the vestry. The copyist ended the Fridays, heard the box ring early, saw the fox's rag-wrapped pocket. **Costs standing:** the "mimo, read the spike" tag is gone; the boy no longer runs for the box; quill's name is in a second book, and the warden's mark no longer opens the lamplighter's page for quill. Lesson kept: let a cost land on an earned asset, not just the fiction (Modulo journal 11-07).
